stimulus: "I can see what you want to argue by the conclusion; I'm less sure the opening promises the same thing."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Do you think the essay is long enough overall, or should I add another paragraph?
options.B: So the introduction needs to set up the claim the conclusion actually makes.
options.C: Great, so the draft is basically fine and I only need to fix a few sentences.
options.D: Right, the conclusion is the part I worked hardest on, so I'm glad it came through.

stimulus: "Have you thought about taking the statistics requirement over the summer instead of piling it on this fall?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Yes, I've thought about statistics quite a lot lately.
options.B: The summer sessions here run for six weeks.
options.C: I would be delighted to enroll at your earliest convenience.
options.D: I hadn't, actually — that would take a lot of pressure off my fall term.

stimulus: "I can put you on the waitlist today; whether a seat actually opens before add/drop closes is another matter."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Perfect, so I'm registered — for the course now.
options.B: Let's do the waitlist, then. What should I line up as a backup if it doesn't clear?
options.C: Add/drop closes on the second Friday, doesn't it?

stimulus: "You may be thinking of the work-study rate — student assistants on the general payroll start a little lower."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Right, so the work-study rate is the lower of the two.
options.B: Are you saying I've been overpaid since the start of the term?
options.C: I appreciate you drawing my attention to this discrepancy in the payroll.
options.D: Oh, I had those two mixed up. What does the general rate come out to?

stimulus: "I don't want to be unfair to Emeka — he did show up to the meeting, just, you know, at the very end."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: He got in at around four-fifteen, I think — or perhaps a little later than that.
options.B: I noticed that too. Should one of us say something before the next meeting?
options.C: Right, so he was there in the end. That's really the thing that counts, isn't it?
options.D: You're being completely unfair to him there, honestly — he did turn up in the end.

stimulus: "You've been at that catalogue terminal a while — the subject headings in that field are a bit unusual."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: I am most grateful to you for your kind solicitude in this matter.
options.B: No, the terminal itself seems to be working perfectly well, thanks for asking.
options.C: Yes, I've been sitting at it about forty minutes now, maybe a little longer.
options.D: They really are — could you show me which heading covers coastal ecology?

stimulus: "You can count the seminar toward the minor, but not toward the language requirement — those are separate lists."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Good, so the seminar takes care of the language requirement and I can skip that list.
options.B: I see — so I still need a language course on top of the seminar.
options.C: Separate lists? That seems like pointless bureaucracy for a single seminar course.
options.D: How many seminars am I allowed to count toward the minor in a single term?

stimulus: "Your technique has come a long way — I'd still like to see you label the tubes before you pipette, though."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Which pipette should I be using for the buffer?
options.B: Thanks — I'll keep working the same way I have been.
options.C: Awesome, so I'm basically done with training then?
options.D: Understood. I'll label everything before I start from now on.

stimulus: "The credit card does sound useful, though I'm honestly trying not to add anything new to my plate this year."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: It is a useful card, yes — and the cashback applies to groceries and fuel as well.
options.B: Please be advised that declining this offer may affect the terms available to you in future.
options.C: So you'd never want a card with us at all. I'll close the application entirely.
options.D: Of course, I'll make a note on your file so nobody rings you about it again.

stimulus: "Have you thought about whether Chapter Three might work better as an appendix?"
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: No, I have not given that any thought at all so far.
options.B: Should the appendix come before or after the bibliography — in the final draft?
options.C: I hadn't, but I can see the case. It is mostly supporting data.
options.D: Chapter Three was definitely the hardest one to write.

stimulus: "The online system won't take a late registration, though there is a paper route most students never hear about."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Could you walk me through the paper route? I'd rather not lose the term.
options.B: How many students registered late this year?
options.C: I would be exceedingly obliged if you might expound upon that.
options.D: Then I'll try the online system once more this evening.

stimulus: "I'm sorry to spring this on you, but the committee needs your revised prospectus by Monday morning."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Yeah, no worries at all — Monday's totally chill for me.
options.B: No problem at all — and I'm sorry for springing this on you at the last minute.
options.C: Which of the committee members will actually be reading the prospectus?
options.D: That's tight, but I can get it to you Monday if the last section stays rough.

stimulus: "Your presentation was clear and well-paced; I'd only say the data slide went by faster than anyone could read it."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Fair point. I'll hold that slide longer and cut the text down.
options.B: Glad it worked — I'll run the same slides again at Thursday's session.
options.C: Thanks — that data slide took me the longest to put together.
options.D: Ugh, I knew that whole data slide was garbage.

stimulus: "Dinner on Saturday sounds great — could I let you know by Thursday? My sister may be flying in."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Your sister is very welcome to join us as well — where is she flying in from, and when?
options.B: Great, I'll put you down as a firm yes for Saturday dinner, then.
options.C: Please confirm your attendance no later than close of business on Thursday.
options.D: Thursday works. I'll hold a seat for you and you can just say the word either way.

stimulus: "Sorry — I think that's rung up as the large. I actually asked for the medium latte."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: The large is only forty cents more, so it's usually the better value.
options.B: You're right, my mistake so I'll refund the difference and remake it as a medium.
options.C: No problem at all, I'll make you another large straight away.
options.D: We regret any inconvenience — and thank you for bringing this matter to our attention.

stimulus: "That's kind of you, but honestly — if you could just watch the bags for a minute, that would help far more."
question: Which is the most natural reply?

options.A: Sure, I'll sit here with them. Take your time.
options.B: I don't mind at all. Which platform were you heading to?
options.C: I accept responsibility for your luggage for the duration of your absence.
options.D: No trouble at all — let me carry the big one up the stairs for you.
